Just think about how, when you click a single key on your keyboard, a you're physically interrupting a little signal that gets recorded by a hardware device in your keyboard, which then interprets which key was pressed and passes it on to the logic controller, which then passes that message to the windowserver, which then uses the scheduler to figure out which window your key was pressed on, which then passes that message to the application controlling the window, which then sends the keypress to the HTML to handle it (if on a web browser), which then applies CSS to format the keypress adequately, and then uses javascript to manipulate the keypress. During this proces, the display system redraws the screen about 50 times a second, so that your keypress appears almost instantaneouly on the screen.

Then you press the submit button, and your web browser packages and encrypts the text that you type into a envelope that includes HTTP headers (as an address) and then just shoots it into the internet, hoping that it reaches your target. Your encrypted message is passed from computer to computer, with DNS translating the desination address at every stage, and eventually, you finally reach the destination server. Your package passes through some firewalls, and is then unencrypted by voat.co using the session key, and it uses your return address to understand that you want to post this under your account, and in /v/askvoat.

Then it saves the message you sent to its database, so that the next time someone looks at /v/askvoat, they see your elaborate request for internet gratification.
